items.transcript: This might be the coolest thing you see today. Uber Eats just started delivering food by drone. And this little pot right here is literally lowering somebody's order into their yard on a string. It went live this week just outside of Houston. And they're saying your food shows up in under 10 minutes with no extra fee and no need to tip, which makes sense because the drone never actually gets within 300 ft of you. It's built by a company called Zipline and it hovers about a football field up, drops this pod down on a tether, sets your food on the grass, and then reels it back up. And I love why they do that, too, because Zipline says most delivery drones come down to about 30 ft. But when this one's way up there, it's about as quiet as a flock of birds, which I mean, you know, kind of depends on the birds, too. Now, Dallas is up next, and they claim they want a million of these a day by 2029. This company, Zipline, got its start flying blood to hospitals in Rwanda, and now it's flying sandwiches to the suburbs. So share this with a friend who loves drones and click that follow button to see the coolest tech every day.
